risks.title: Commodity Price Volatility
risks.score_rationale: EOG is directly exposed to oil and gas price volatility. In 2025, NYMEX crude prices declined 14% to $64.78/barrel while gas prices rose 51% to $3.43/MMBtu, directly impacting revenues and net income (down 22%).

risks.title: Reserve Management and Replacement
risks.score_rationale: EOG's long-term viability depends on its ability to maintain and replace reserves. Although reserves increased by 12% in 2025 (766 MMBoe), a prolonged decline would threaten future operations.

risks.title: Geopolitical and Regulatory Risks
risks.score_rationale: EOG operates primarily in the U.S. (99% of reserves), Trinidad (1%), and new projects in Bahrain and the UAE. Political changes, sanctions, or regulatory shifts could impact resource access and profitability.

risks.title: Environmental and Energy Transition Risks
risks.score_rationale: As an oil and gas producer, EOG faces operational environmental risks (spills, accidents) and long-term risks associated with the transition to a low-carbon economy.

risks.title: Market and Demand Risks
risks.score_rationale: Global oil and gas demand is subject to changes driven by economic, technological, and political factors, as well as trade policies (tariffs, trade barriers noted in the 10-K).

risks.title: Liquidity and Capital Structure
risks.score_rationale: Although EOG maintains a strong liquidity position ($3.4B cash + $3.0B credit facility), the $4.5B debt issuance (four tranches in July and November 2025) for the Encino acquisition increases financial leverage and exposure to future interest rates.

ai_positioning.summary: The company did not mention AI or machine learning in the provided excerpts. Its primary business appears to be in the energy sector.
